description: Table II is a printed three-line-style data table (no micrographs or plots) headed "Tensile properties cast Fe-30Mn-9Al-XSi-0.9C steels with different melt practices". Seven columns are printed: Wt.% Si, Wt.% P, Heat treatment, Hardness Brinell^a (sub-headed "No Calcium treatment"), 0.2% YS (MPa), UTS (MPa) and % elongation^b. The body is divided by full-width sub-headers into three melt practices: rows with no calcium treatment (Si 1.0-1.4 wt%, P 0.06 wt%) given either "Solution treated at 1050°C" 2 h or "Aged at 530°C" 10 h and 30 h; "Calcium treated with Ar stirring" (Si 0.78, 1.07, 1.56 wt%; P 0.007-0.001 wt%), including one "As-cast" row with no Brinell value, plus solution-treated (2 h) and aged at 530°C (20, 26, 60 h) rows; and "Calcium treated only" (Si 1.01 wt%, P 0.006 wt%) aged at 530°C (22, 60 h) and 570°C (4, 10 h). Values span Brinell 197-384, 0.2% YS 450-1016 MPa, UTS 687-1085 MPa and elongation 5-64%, with ± standard deviations printed only for the calcium-treated rows. The table shows that ageing at 530°C raises YS/UTS and hardness while lowering elongation, that higher Si raises strength, and that calcium treatment with low P markedly improves elongation.

subfigures.description: Single-panel data table (Table II) with columns Wt.% Si, Wt.% P, Heat treatment, Hardness Brinell (No Calcium treatment), 0.2% YS (MPa), UTS (MPa), % elongation; grouped by melt practice (no calcium treatment; Calcium treated with Ar stirring; Calcium treated only) and heat treatment (solution treated at 1050°C, aged at 530°C, aged at 570°C, as-cast).

observations.observation: The table header lists seven columns: Wt.% Si, Wt.% P, Heat treatment, Hardness Brinell (No Calcium treatment), 0.2% YS (MPa), UTS (MPa) and % elongation.
The no-calcium-treatment rows have Si 1.0 and 1.4 wt% and P 0.06 wt%; solution treated at 1050°C for 2 h gives 458/549 MPa YS, 687/766 MPa UTS and 44/36% elongation.
Ageing the no-calcium heats at 530°C for 10 h raises YS to 891-922 MPa and UTS to 940-995 MPa while elongation falls to 18-14%.
For the no-calcium heats, 30 h at 530°C gives the highest values, 1005-1016 MPa YS, 1065-1085 MPa UTS and only 8-5% elongation.
In the 'Calcium treated with Ar stirring' block, the as-cast row (Si 0.78 wt%, P 0.007 wt%) has no Brinell hardness printed and shows 616 MPa YS, 698 MPa UTS and 17% elongation.
Solution treatment at 1050°C for 2 h after calcium treatment with Ar stirring gives the highest ductility in the table, 64% elongation at both Si 1.07 and 1.56 wt% with UTS 737 and 733 MPa.
Uncertainties (± one standard deviation) are printed only in the calcium-treated blocks; the no-calcium rows carry single values with no error bars.
Calcium treated with Ar stirring, aged at 530°C: at 60 h Si 1.56 wt% reaches 937 ± 8.9 MPa YS and 1016 ± 2.5 MPa UTS, the highest UTS in the table.
'Calcium treated only' (Si 1.01 wt%, P 0.006 wt%) aged at 570°C gives lower strength than equivalent 530°C ageing: 666 ± 37 MPa YS at 4 h falling to 804 MPa at 10 h with UTS 757 ± 27 MPa and 877 MPa.
Across all blocks, hardness (Brinell), 0.2% YS and UTS increase with ageing time while % elongation decreases.
The caption states the steel nominal composition is Fe-30Mn-9Al-XSi-0.9C cast steels with different melt practices.
The caption states hardness Brinell (3000 kg) values were converted from Rockwell B and C scale measurements.
The caption states elongation was measured over a 25.4-mm (1-in.) gage length and that uncertainty is one standard deviation reported for test samples greater than two.
